notes:
Doc-only PR replacing stale or relative file references with full Mathlib paths. For every changed object I read the file as the PR leaves it, checked that each new path exists in the reviewed tree (file_read on the target), checked the other file and declaration references in the same comment or docstring, and checked the 100-character line limit on rewrapped lines. Proof-golf, generalization and naming do not apply: no statement, proof or declaration name changes. All four proposed edits compile with lean_verify_edit (comment-only changes).

- module_doc in Bicategory/Functor/StrictPseudofunctor.lean: `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Bicategory/Functor/Strict.lean` exists and is a `deprecated_module (since := "2025-10-02")` re-exporting `Bicategory/Strict/Pseudofunctor`, so the TODO now names the right file (there is no `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Functor/Strict.lean`). Lines within 100 chars. Nothing to ask.
- module_doc in ConcreteCategory/Bundled.lean: `ConcreteCategory/UnbundledHom.lean`, `ConcreteCategory/BundledHom.lean` and `ConcreteCategory/Basic.lean` all exist, and the old `HasForget/...` paths were wrong. `Bundled` itself is not deprecated, so the "will be deprecated" note still holds. Rewrap fine. Nothing to ask.
- CategoryTheory.BundledHom and CategoryTheory.UnbundledHom (one family: identical deprecation-message edits): the full path inside the `@[deprecated "..."]` string is correct, the string continuation and `since` date are unchanged, and the lines fit. Attributes otherwise unchanged. Nothing to ask.
- section comment in Functor/Basic.lean: the new reference is correct, since `Mathlib/Tactic/CategoryTheory/Reassoc.lean` does `public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Basic`. But the same file still has a bare, stale reference at line 130 (`Whiskering.lean`): the unitor isos now live in `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Functor/Category.lean`, and `Whiskering.lean` only uses them. Finding 1.
- module_doc in Groupoid/Subgroupoid.lean: `Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Subgroup/Basic.lean` exists and `Mathlib/GroupTheory/Subgroup/Basic.lean` does not. `Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Subgraph.lean` exists. Line is 97 chars. Nothing to ask.
- module_doc in Limits/FunctorCategory/Filtered.lean and Finite.lean (one family): `Limits/FunctorCategory/Basic.lean` exists. The other referenced files (`Limits/Filtered.lean`, `Limits/Shapes/FiniteProducts.lean`) exist. Lines are 98 chars. Nothing to ask.
- docstring before colimit.ι_desc in Limits/HasLimits.lean: `Mathlib/Tactic/CategoryTheory/Reassoc.lean` is the right successor of the Lean 3 `Tactic/reassoc_axiom.lean`. The other refs in this file (`Adjunction/Limits.lean`, `Limits/ConeCategory.lean`) exist. Nothing to ask.
- module_doc in Limits/Preserves/Limits.lean: the directory reference is correct; `Preserves/Shapes/` exists (e.g. `Shapes/Terminal` is imported by ConeCategory). The same module doc, two lines up, names declarations that do not exist: `preservesLimitsIso` (actual `preservesLimitIso`), `Limit F` (actual `limit F`) and `PreservesLimit.preserves t` (actual `isLimitOfPreserves G t`, see `preserves_lift_mapCone` at line 44). Finding 3.
- module_doc in Limits/Preserves/Over.lean: `Comma/Over/Pullback.lean` exists and holds `Over.forgetAdjStar`, the successor of the removed `Adjunction/Over.lean`. But `forgetAdjStar` lives in `section HasBinaryProducts`, while the note says without qualification that `Over.forget X` preserves all colimits because it is a left adjoint. The trailing period is also missing. Finding 4.
- module_doc in Localization/Equivalence.lean: the path is fixed and the rewrap fits (97 chars max). The rewrapped sentence still names `Localization.of_equivalence_target`, but the lemma is `Functor.IsLocalization.of_equivalence_target` (Predicate.lean line 393, inside `namespace Functor` / `namespace IsLocalization`). Likewise, `of_equivalence_source` and `of_equivalences` in this very file are `Functor.IsLocalization.*`; `Localization.isEquivalence` is correct. There is also a grammar slip ("which provide"). Finding 2.
- module_doc in Monoidal/Mon_.lean: `Monoidal/Braided/Basic.lean` exists and defines `tensorμ`, `leftUnitor_monoidal`, `rightUnitor_monoidal` and `associator_monoidal`, so both edits are right. The other refs (`Tactic/Attr/Register.lean`, `Monoidal/Internal/Module.lean`) exist. Nothing to ask.
- Scope: the edits match the title. Other stale bare refs exist elsewhere in CategoryTheory (e.g. `Comma/Basic.lean` "`Over.lean`", `Functor/Category.lean` "`Currying.lean`"), but they are outside the changed files, so I ask nothing there.

findings.claim: The comment before `Functor.comp_id` / `Functor.id_comp` in `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Functor/Basic.lean` (a file this PR edits to fix references) still has a bare, stale reference: "Natural isomorphisms are also provided in `Whiskering.lean`." The isomorphisms `Functor.leftUnitor` and `Functor.rightUnitor` are defined in `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Functor/Category.lean` (lines 158/166), not in `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Whiskering.lean`, which only uses them.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace line 130 with `-- Natural isomorphisms are also provided in `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Functor/Category.lean`` followed by `-- (`Functor.rightUnitor` and `Functor.leftUnitor`).`, matching the full-path convention used in the rest of this PR.

findings.claim: The module docstring of `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Localization/Equivalence.lean`, which this PR rewraps, names lemmas that do not exist: `Localization.of_equivalence_target` is `Functor.IsLocalization.of_equivalence_target` (Predicate.lean, inside `namespace Functor.IsLocalization`), and `Localization.of_equivalence_source` and `Localization.of_equivalences`, declared in this very file, are `Functor.IsLocalization.of_equivalence_source` and `Functor.IsLocalization.of_equivalences`. So the references neither resolve nor link in the docs. The sentence also says "which provide" for "which provides".
findings.suggested_fix: In the module doc, write `Functor.IsLocalization.of_equivalence_target`, `Functor.IsLocalization.of_equivalence_source` and `Functor.IsLocalization.of_equivalences` in place of the three `Localization.*` names, keep `Localization.isEquivalence`, change "which provide" to "which provides", and rewrap to 100 columns (checked: it compiles and every line fits).

findings.claim: The module docstring of `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Preserves/Limits.lean`, whose last sentence this PR fixes, still has stale names two lines above. It says `preservesLimitsIso : G.obj (Limit F) ≅ Limit (F ⋙ G)`, but the declaration is `preservesLimitIso : G.obj (limit F) ≅ limit (F ⋙ G)` (line 53). It also writes `(PreservesLimit.preserves t).lift`, an API that no longer exists: the file's `preserves_lift_mapCone` states `(isLimitOfPreserves G t).lift (G.mapCone c₂) = G.map (t.lift c₂)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Change line 14 to `canonical isomorphism `preservesLimitIso : G.obj (limit F) ≅ limit (F ⋙ G)`.` and line 16 to ``(isLimitOfPreserves G t).lift (G.mapCone c₂) = G.map (t.lift c₂)` (`preserves_lift_mapCone`).`.

findings.claim: The module docstring of `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/Preserves/Over.lean` now points to `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Comma/Over/Pullback.lean`, but it still says without qualification that `Over.forget X` "already preserves all colimits because it is a left adjoint". The adjunction there, `Over.forgetAdjStar`, and the `(forget X).IsLeftAdjoint` instance hold only under `[HasBinaryProducts C]` (its own docstring says the assumption is necessary), while this file's instances assume nothing on `C`. The reference also gives a file but no declaration, and the sentence lacks a final period.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite lines 14-15 as: `Note that `Over.forget X : Over X ⥤ C` already preserves all colimits when `C` has binary products,` / `because it is then a left adjoint (`Over.forgetAdjStar`, see` / ``Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Comma/Over/Pullback.lean`).` (checked: it compiles and fits in 100 columns).
